# Edges models

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_docs.py from the model cards; do not edit. -->

8 edges models. Each section says what the model is, whether it may be used commercially and how fast it is; licences and checks are under Details.

Input: one RGB image. Output: a line / edge map `[H, W]` in [0, 1] at the input size (1 = line), the ControlNet preprocessors (line art, HED, PiDiNet, TEED / Anyline); M-LSD also returns straight line segments.

Measured on RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130; `fastforks bench MODEL --size HxW` measures yours. The summary uses one input, 1080x1920: kernels time with its speed-up over the faster original run, and kernels peak reserved memory with its ratio to the smaller original one. Where measured (one variant per family), a variant's table also lists portable under `torch.compile` and the fp16 TensorRT engine of portable ([export](../export.md); memory: the engine's device memory + torch's peak). – = not measured; no kernels = the family has no kernels backend (reason under its table). Reserved memory is the allocator's cache: kernels (CUDA graphs, cuDNN workspaces) can reserve a few percent to some tens of percent more than portable at the same allocated peak.

Other devices: [Apple M1 Pro 16 GB](../devices/apple-m1-pro-16gb.md), [Apple M1 Pro 16 GB (MLX)](../devices/apple-m1-pro-mlx-16gb.md), [NVIDIA L4](../devices/l4-22gb.md), [NVIDIA L40S](../devices/l40s-44gb.md), [NVIDIA A10](../devices/a10-22gb.md), [NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB](../devices/a100-sxm4-40gb.md), [NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000](../devices/rtx-pro-6000-96gb.md); [across devices](../benchmarks.md#other-devices).

| model | commercial | kernels time (ms),<br>speed-up vs original | kernels peak memory (MiB, reserved),<br>ratio to original |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`anyline`](#anyline) | yes | 18.8, 15.9x (1024x1024) | 384, 0.68x |
| [`hed`](#hed) | yes | 4.44, 4.6x (1024x1024) | 146, 0.65x |
| [`lineart`](#lineart) | yes | 8.49, 1.9x (1024x1024) | 186, 1.0x |

## AnyLine line art

AnyLine (TheMisto.ai): sharp line maps for line-conditioned ControlNets such as MistoLine, from the MTEED edge network blended with a line art of the image. MIT code; OpenRAIL++-M weights (commercial use with use restrictions).

Commercial use: yes.

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `anyline` | synthetic (1080x1920) | original<br>portable<br>kernels | 585<br>47.4<br>– | 909 / 1002<br>654 / 722<br>– |
| `anyline` | synthetic (1024x1024) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 299<br>21.0<br>18.8<br>11.6<br>12.9 (full line map only; memory estimated) | 509 / 562<br>362 / 384<br>362 / 384<br>306 / 346<br>528 / 542 |

### Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 0.002 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.02 and p99 <= 0.25 (absolute error of the output `edges`).

| variant | kernels error vs original, mean / p99 | GPU, torch | kernels used |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anyline` | 8e-05 / 2e-05 | RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.10.0+cu130 | `edge_components@d6becc089ab3:sm_120` |

### Limitations

- Layers are blended in float as TheMistoAI/ComfyUI-Anyline; controlnet_aux's `AnylineDetector` blends uint8 arrays, where `1 - (1 - top) * (1 - base)` wraps around, so its maps differ wherever line art is drawn.

</details>

## M-LSD line segments

M-LSD (NAVER, AAAI 2022): finds the straight line segments of a photo (rooms, buildings) with a small MobileNetV2 network and draws them as a 1-pixel line map for the MLSD ControlNet; returns the segments too. Apache-2.0 code and weights.

Commercial use: yes.

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mlsd` | synthetic (1080x1920) | original<br>portable<br>kernels | 35.6<br>9.33<br>– | 185 / 212<br>127 / 170<br>– |
| `mlsd` | synthetic (1024x1024) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp32 | 20.6<br>7.65<br>7.03<br>4.61<br>5.75 (standalone CNN with eager resize and line decoding) | 113 / 132<br>72 / 90<br>72 / 90<br>101 / 130<br>295 / 310 |

All 102 YorkUrban images in the DT-LSD release. Each M-LSD mode uses 512-pixel short-side detection, cubic resizing, a score and length threshold of 0.1, and up to 200 segments. Structural AP matches endpoints on a 256 x 256 coordinate grid, testing both endpoint orders and matching each annotation at most once. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

PiDiNet (Su et al., ICCV 2021): a small, fast edge detector with pixel-difference convolutions, folded into plain convolutions here; soft edges for the soft-edge ControlNet. Research use only (non-commercial).

## TEED edges

TEED (Soria et al., 2023): a tiny edge detector (58 k parameters) that draws soft edge maps for the soft-edge ControlNet, quantized to a few levels by default. MIT code and weights (trained on BIPED, a research-use dataset; see the card).

Commercial use: yes.
